content.key_idea: Large model training depends on a layered stack from user code and training frameworks down through GPU/CPU/interconnect hardware to the inter-host network, and a fault in any layer can cause performance issues.
content.reading_order: Top-down through three labeled layers: In the container (user code and framework operations), Physical host (hardware), and Inter-host (network).

evidence: Large model training (LMT) requires the cooperation of multiple hardware and software modules (Figure 1)
Software modules include GPU operators, communication libraries like NCCL

summary: This is a background figure showing the full stack involved in executing large model training (LMT). It is drawn as three flat, color-coded horizontal bands stacked top to bottom. The top band, labeled 'In the container', shows the user's code running atop a training framework (Megatron, DeepSpeed, Nemo), which issues GPU operations, CPU/memory operations, and collective communication. The middle band, labeled 'Physical host', shows the corresponding hardware: GPUs, CPU/memory/disk, and NVLink/PCIe/NICs. The bottom band, labeled 'Inter-host', shows the inter-host network connecting multiple physical hosts. The figure has no arrows; it simply enumerates the layers that must all function correctly for LMT to run without performance issues, motivating the paper's claim that malfunctions in any layer can cause slowdowns.
summary_zh: 该图展示大模型训练所依赖的完整软硬件栈：容器内的用户代码与训练框架（发起 GPU、CPU/内存与集合通信操作），物理主机的 GPU、CPU/内存/磁盘及 NVLink/PCIe/NIC 硬件，以及主机间网络，三层平铺自上而下排列。
